item.title: BE ALERT - AN OVERLAND FLOOD WATCH HAS BEEN ISSUED BY MANITOBA'S HYDROLOGIC FORECAST CENTRE
item.description:
Seasonal Overland Flooding Warning | An Overland Flood Watch Has Been Issued By Manitoba's Hydrologic Forecast Centre |

From September 6 to 8, a system may bring 50 to 70 mm of precipitation to areas already impacted by significant rainfall. Water levels may increase along the Swan River, Qu'appelle River, Assiniboine River, Shell River, and in the Parkland Region. Heavy rainfall over a short period may lead to high surface runoff and overland flooding. Up-to-date information is available at https://manitoba.ca/floodinfo/ and www.manitoba511.ca

| Moderate - possible threat | Immediate - act now | Pine River, Manitoba

item.title: Souris Hospital parking lot paving work set to begin next week
item.description:
Souris Hospital parking lot paving work set to begin next week jenniferdhogan Fri, 09/04/2026 - 14:08

Paving work at the Souris Hospital parking lot is set to begin Tuesday, September 8 and is expected to be completed within approximately four weeks, weather permitting.

The south side parking lot will be closed during this time and patients that typically park there are asked to use the main lot. Staff will also be directed to park in an alternative area. The south side parking lot will remain inaccessible until the paving work has been completed.

To ensure the safety of patients, visitors, and staff, signage will be in place throughout the project to help direct vehicles and pedestrians.

Patients and visitors are encouraged to plan ahead, allow extra time for parking, and follow all posted signage and directions from traffic control personnel. 

Health PEI appreciates the public's patience and cooperation as this work is completed to improve the hospital parking area.

item.title: Province seeks proposals for long-term care beds in Kings County
item.description:
Province seeks proposals for long-term care beds in Kings County jenniferdhogan Fri, 09/04/2026 - 11:40

The Government of Prince Edward Island announced today that plans are moving forward to expand long-term care capacity in Kings County through a public Request for Proposals (RFP).

The RFP seeks qualified private operators to develop and operate up to 48 new long-term care beds in Kings County. This project builds on recent awards for 140 private long-term care beds in Cornwall and Summerside and supports government’s ongoing efforts to meet the growing demand for long-term care across the province. 

“We’ve committed to expanding long-term care capacity and we're taking action on that commitment here in Kings County. This is about making sure people have access to high-quality care close to home. We know the need is growing, and we’re planning ahead so that care is there when people need it.”

- Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle

Adding long-term care capacity also supports the health care system by helping patients move to the right care setting when they no longer require hospital care. More capacity also benefits people with complex needs who are waiting at home for placement in long-term care. 

The Nursing Home Association of PEI (NHAPEI) represents private nursing homes across the province and is a valued partner in supporting the delivery of quality long-term care.

“The Nursing Home Association of PEI is extremely pleased with the plans for long-term care expansion in the Kings area,” said executive director Darlene Oakes. “We hear from potential residents who wish to stay close to their hometown, and families strongly prefer that their loved ones remain in the local area. This allows residents to stay connected to their communities and participate in activities that are important to them. We look forward to collaborating with government and Health PEI to make this a reality for Kings County.”  

The deadline to submit proposals is October 9, 2026. This RFP is issued on behalf of the Health PEI Provincial Long-Term Care Program.

For more information, visit Tender Opportunity | Long-Term Care Beds

item.title: Anti-Racism Microgrant funding available for community-led projects
item.description:
Anti-Racism Microgrant funding available for community-led projects jpranahan Thu, 09/03/2026 - 15:11

Applications are open for the 2026-2027 round of the Anti-Racism Microgrant with a total of $100,000 in funding available.

The microgrant supports PEI’s anti-racism goals by funding small, community-based initiatives and enhancing larger projects that work to remove barriers affecting racialized and Indigenous peoples. 

Lasting change takes time and happens in stages. These grants support early planning, start-up activities and important steps within larger efforts. The funding helps individuals, organizations and communities reduce racial barriers, build skills and resources and support lasting positive change across Prince Edward Island.

Eligible projects must align with one or more of the following goals: 

  • Making changes to policies, practices, and organizations to remove barriers and address systemic racism 
  • Strengthening the ability of organizations and public institutions to advance anti-racism efforts
  • Empowering BIPOC communities by building partnerships, advocating for change and leading community-led research
  • Advancing public awareness, community engagement and advocacy efforts that address racism 
  • Strengthening BIPOC community networks, leadership, and involvement in public life and decision-making

Projects must promote anti-racism education and awareness, community support, capacity-building and improve organizational governance.

Funding is available through three streams:

  • Youth, aged 14 to 24, can apply for amounts ranging from $100 to $1,500
  • Individuals, aged 25 and over, can apply for amounts ranging from $100 to $2,000
  • Non-profit organizations and professional associations can apply for amounts ranging from $1,000 to $5,000

Applications will be accepted until 11:59 p.m. on October 2, 2026.

Quotes:

“We’re pleased to offer another round of microgrants that empower individual and organizations to advance anti-racism efforts in their communities. Each year, we receive many applications and we look forward to supporting these efforts as we work toward a more inclusive PEI, free from discrimination and racism.” 

- Premier Rob Lantz

“The Anti-Racism Table is proud to see the ongoing interest in the microgrants. We are inspired by the innovative ways communities across PEI are working to break down racial barriers in PEI and bring people together through education and awareness.” 

 - Co-Chair of the PEI Anti-Racism Table Brad Cooper  

“The Anti-Racism Microgrant allowed Women’s Network PEI to work with Seed Room Consulting to examine our organizational policies and systems through an anti-racist and equity-focused lens. The project helped us identify gaps and develop practical tools and response guidelines to better address harm, strengthen accountability, and create a safer, more equitable organization.”

- Women’s Network PEI executive director Jacki Freamo 

“The Anti-Racism Microgrant empowered the UPEI Student Union to host transformative workshops on mental health, systemic racism, and community wellbeing. Post-workshop surveys revealed that 82–87 per cent of participants gained a deeper understanding of systemic racism, while up to 80 per cent reported increased confidence in practicing allyship and supporting peers. This initiative meaningfully strengthened campus inclusion and student belonging.”

- UPEI Student Union president Amy Cristina Montesdeoca Castro 

To apply, and for more information about the microgrant, visit Anti-Racism Microgrants.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”
